description:
FILED s473r (2026-09-07) as the OTHER HALF of #1189`s finding, measured.

WHAT #1189 FOUND.  Every emitted program opens with the package preamble for
each package it mentions â and the program a STRING EVAL produces is an
emitted program.  So a module that generates code at run time re-runs BOTH
halves of that preamble for things that already exist.  Counted by
encapsulating the entry points and running `moo-objs` at two N:

    per iteration:  12 x defpackage   and   12 x ensure-class
      10 of each for Method::Generate::Accessor::_Generated (Moo`s Sub::Quote
      eval package), 2 of each for Pt

s473r SHIPPED the defpackage half (`%p-package-ready-p`, runtime only):
moo-objs 1.9986 -> 1.2193 s, 38.15x perl -> 29.59x.  THIS TASK IS THE OTHER
HALF: `(defclass plc-x () ())`, which pl2cl writes LITERALLY into the emitted
file (Pl/Parser.pm, the "Emit (p-defpackage) and (defclass) inline" site), so
it cannot be guarded from the runtime.

THE RESIDUE, measured after the defpackage fix (sb-sprof :cpu 1 ms, N=20000
vs 60000, per-function self deltas renormalised over the positives â the
package machinery is GONE from the table and this is what is left):

    4.6 %  (lambda (sb-pcl::.arg0.) :in "SYS:SRC;PCL;BRAID.LISP")
    3.8 %  call-with-recursive-lock
    3.4 %  call-with-system-mutex
    3.2 %  sb-kernel:%member-eq
    2.4 %  sb-pcl::update-ctors
    2.1 %  sb-impl::puthash/any
    2.0 %  shared-initialize
    2.0 %  DLISP3 dfun
    ... nothing above 4.6 %; the sb-pcl entries together are ~35 % of the loop

THE FIX SHAPE: emit `(p-defclass plc-x (SUPER...))` instead of the bare
`defclass`, with a runtime macro that skips when the class is ALREADY there
with the SAME direct superclasses.  The superclass comparison is
load-bearing, not decoration: a program can define one package twice with a
different @ISA, and a guard keyed on mere existence would freeze the first
one`s parents.  `sb-mop:class-direct-superclasses` on the found class,
compared by class NAME against the form`s list, is the test.

BAR (an emission change, so the full boat): generation bump + the three
artifacts; corpus-diff with every differing file explained (every emitted
program has a preamble, so this touches ALL of them â the explanation is ONE
shape); emission-ab over the wide list with RCDIFF 0; ir-host-leak (the
emission loses a bare CL `defclass` and gains a `p-â¦` head, which is a leak
REMOVED); the full sweep; and guard rows for the negatives â a class
re-opened with a DIFFERENT @ISA must still re-run, a class re-opened with the
SAME @ISA must not, and `Pl/t/perf-levers-04.t`s nine perl answers for
re-opened packages and string evals must all stay.

PRIZE: ~35 % of `moo-objs` loop samples, i.e. plausibly another 1.22 -> ~0.9 s
and 29.6x perl -> ~22x.  Sized but NOT taken by s473r: it is an emission
change and the round had already shipped two runtime levers.

=== DONE (s473s, 2026-09-08) — SHIPPED, and the PREMISE MEASURED FALSE ===

`p-defclass` is in: an exported macro that expands to the `defclass` only when
`%p-class-ready-p` says the class is NOT already there with exactly those
direct superclasses.  Seven emission sites (Pl/Parser.pm x6, Pl/Parser2.pm x1)
write it; generation v2-1030 -> v2-1060; the three artifacts regenerated;
`docs/ir-op-inventory.{tsv,md}` +1 row; ir-spec §7.3 (with an example), §11b's
kernel row and §12b's preamble list updated.  Guard `Pl/t/defclass-01.t`
(12 rows, 0.6 s), inverse-verified on the c2016433 extraction (11 of 12 fail
there; the 12th is the perl-level program, whose ANSWER must not change).
`Pl/t/parser2-01.t` test 57 was a stale guard asserting the literal
`(defclass` text and was fixed in the same commit (s416 rule).

THE PRIZE THIS TASK NAMED IS NOT THERE, and it was measured rather than
explained away.  The filing read #1189's finding as "12 `ensure-class`
executions per `moo-objs` loop iteration", by analogy with the `p-defpackage`
half s473r shipped.  A quiet-box emission A/B read `moo-objs` **+2.3 %** — no
win — so both readiness tests were counted on the same program (wrappers
around `%p-package-ready-p` / `%p-class-ready-p`):

    moo-objs N=500    CLASS ready=0 made=20  |  PKG ready=6096  made=62
    moo-objs N=2000   CLASS ready=0 made=20  |  PKG ready=24096 made=62
    evalpkg  N=500    CLASS ready=0 made=1   |  PKG ready=1500  made=3
    evalpkg  N=2000   CLASS ready=0 made=1   |  PKG ready=6000  made=3

The PACKAGE tests are 12 per iteration — exactly #1189's figure — while the
CLASS forms are 20 in total, N-INDEPENDENT, with ZERO hits; and on the shape
this task describes in the abstract (`evalpkg`: a loop that string-evals
`package K1; our @ISA = ("PA"); 1`) it is ONE class form for the whole run.
**The preamble a string eval's program carries declares its PACKAGE and not
its class**, so the re-opening this guard exists for does not occur on either
population.  The +2.3 % is noise by construction: the bench's exec metric is
t(N_BIG) - t(0) and all 20 class forms run at LOAD, inside both terms.

KEPT anyway, for what it does deliver and not for a number: the emitted file
no longer writes a bare host `defclass` (ir-spec §11b — the IR stays in its
own vocabulary), and a class re-opened by any future emission path is free
instead of expensive.  DO NOT re-derive the speed claim; it was measured and
it is zero.  The three places that carried it (the macro's docstring, ir-spec
§7.3, the guard file's header) now name the measurement.


=== THE LOOP HALF PROFILED (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus) â the share, so this task
=== is sized when someone takes it ===

`moo-objs` at N=300 000 through `pcl`'s WARM script cache (so the transpile and
the program's own compile are out of the profile; scratch/s473x/prof-mod.pl in
the s473x worktree), 18 484 samples:

    (WITHOUT-INTERRUPTS-BODY- :in sb-thread::call-with-recursive-lock)
                                          3.1 % self / 64.1 % TOTAL
    sb-thread::call-with-recursive-lock    1.2 self / 62.6 total
    (with-recursive-lock-thunk :in sb-pcl::make-preliminary-layout)
                                           0.9 self / 13.9 total
    (sb-pcl::fast-method shared-initialize (sb-pcl::slot-object t))
                                           3.1 self /  8.4 total
    (SYS:SRC;PCL;BRAID.LISP .arg0.)        3.9 self
    (WITHOUT-INTERRUPTS-BODY- :in call-with-system-mutex)
                                           2.6 self /  9.3 total
    sb-pcl::update-ctors                   1.8 self
    puthash/any 1.7, remhash/any 1.4, gethash/equal 1.3,
    grab-mutex 1.1, release-mutex 1.0, %set-symbol-global-value 1.0

That is CLOS CLASS CREATION UNDER A SYSTEM MUTEX, per iteration â the
`defclass` sibling of #1189's `defpackage` half, exactly as this task says.
It is the dominant group of the loop half.

NOT BUILT by s473x: it is an L by the round's own scale.  #1189 shipped because
`%p-package-ready-p` could ask a cheap, EXACT question about an existing
package (its USE-LIST, through `sb-impl::package-%use-list`, which does not
copy).  The class twin needs the same kind of predicate â "is the class that
exists already what this `defclass` would make" â and getting that wrong is a
silent wrong, not a slow path.  That is a design, and this round's budget was
two S levers.
subject: PERF (the OTHER half of #1189, sized s473r): the emitted package preamble's `(defclass plc-X () ())` is written LITERALLY by pl2cl (Pl/Parser.pm, the "Emit (p-defpackage) and (defclass) inline" site) so a string-eval-produced program re-runs `ensure-class` for a class that already exists -- 12 per `moo-objs` iteration (10 for Moo's Sub::Quote eval package); after s473r's defpackage half (moo-objs 2.00 -> 1.22 s) the residue is ~35 % of the loop in sb-pcl (braid / update-ctors / shared-initialize / mutexes, nothing above 4.6 %); FIX SHAPE = emit a `p-defclass` macro that is a no-op when the class exists (an EMISSION change: gen bump + artifacts + the full boat)
